candidates.description: Includes all known errata and clarifications. (Hovan Du is ID 139.) Removed introductory section "Read this first." Sharpened images. Fixed typos. Removed section headings for charts and tables. This caused renumbering of subsequent sections in some cases. Any references to the charts are by their names. They are being reformatted and will be in a separate upload. Added subsections for each defined term. Added titles for each subsection. Added a subsections for definitions of terms. Removed 11.25 (It said to look for abbreviations in the key to the chart.) and renumbered following sections. 11.5.3 Kamtol (Area III-A): The rule changed the text of the result for rolling a 4 when flying. The effectis are the same (roll again as walking), so I deleted that part of the rule. Made capitalization and wording consistent. Added new charts (and reformated others), especially in the scenarios. They will be added to the separate charts upload where appropriate and referenced to these revised rules. Added table of abbreviations. Larger font, fewer columns, and more white space increased the length of the rules. Removed some of the snarky commentary to save space. (Such as "When you're incomparable, things tend to go your way.") Mirrored margins for those who wish to print two-sided and punch holes. Interactive table of contents (bookmarks) if using in soft copy. Please see my BGG blog and open the comments for my approach to rules. Normally, I don't comment on the rules. I will make an exception here. The author preferred to use the word "should" instead of "if" throghout. Besides being longer, it requires the subjunctive. This is seen more in British English than American English. Edgar Rice Burroughs was American (as am I), so I have changed this construction to if. Please Geek Mail any corrections to me.

The PDF contains print-and-play cards you can print, cut, and sleeve. Or you can roll dice or choose randomly to get the same effect. candidates.title: Risk Rulebook Comparison: 1980's vs. 2008 Revised vs. 2015 Hasbro — A Side-by-Side Field Manual
candidates.description: A 13-page landscape field manual that lays the three modern-era editions of Risk side by side in parallel columns across eleven sections: Game Identity & Scope, Components, Setup & Initial Placement, Turn Structure, Combat Mechanics, Combat Is the Same in All Three Editions (proof page), Cards & Trade-Ins, Game Modes & Variants, Unique Features Spotlight, Where the Editions Actually Differ, and a Bottom Line that recommends which edition to choose for which group. The combat rules turn out to be functionally identical across all three editions — the 1980's "choose dice" framing and the 2008/2015 "send troops" framing reduce to the same procedure under the army-count constraint. Section VI proves this by quoting each rulebook verbatim, then walking the same battle through all three rulebooks to show the state evolves the same way. Most of what differs is structural: Objectives, capitals, cities, Secret Missions, and the different game modes. Aimed at players who own more than one edition, or who are deciding which to buy.

candidates.title: Classification table (PRO rules) - English
candidates.description: Based on the list of rankings by Heiko Doubleu , I created an Excel file for convenient handling of multi-stage races. It is best used with the latest version of the PRO rules . The results of each stage are entered in an individual sheet, from where a separate calculation sheet picks up the data and does the necessary calculations for the overall standings. The general overview page, thus, does not require any manual labour and provides an excellent overview on the results of each stage as well as the classifications in the different categories. I also incorporated 9 stages of the Tour de France 2022 (this one was particularly exciting because one stage contained sections with cobblestones). For this, I recommend using the game board by Ludo Nauws (getting it printed on e.g. tarp may be cheaper than you think). How to use: During a race: - Sprint and climber points are recorded in accordance with the above-mentioned PRO rules. At the end of a race: - Calculate the time difference relative to the race winner (who receives 0 min 0 s) by adding the corresponding numbers in the minutes/seconds columns (refer to PRO rules for how to calculate the time differences). - Enter the final race position of each cyclist (after sprinting). - Enter the left-over energy cards for everyone (relevant for fitness cards in the next race). - Award sprint/climber points depending on the type of race (time trial, flat or mountain stage). Features: - The overview table automatically highlights the leaders in each category (general classification, sprint, climber). - The time of the leader in the general classification is displayed as "0:00" automatically and the deficits of the other riders are calculated relative to that. - The calculation of all three classifications contain tie breakers in the event of equal times or points, respectively. - Bonus seconds for the general classification (awarded for intermediate sprints and top-3 finishes) are awarded and calculated automatically. - The team classification only considers the best three riders. If you notice errors, please let me know.

candidates.title: Random Events Table (German)
candidates.description: This is the random events table to go along with the German PRO rules . Like the rules, the table was initially created by ParisRoubaix . Es gibt zwei Versionen der Tabelle: Die ursprüngliche Variante A bezieht die Teamwertung mit ein, so dass Teams, die im Ranking weiter hinten stehen, eine höhere Wahrscheinlichkeit haben, dass ihre Fahrer Züge verlieren. Der thematische Gedanke ist, dass die Versorgungsfahrzeuge "schlechterer" Teams weiter hinten fahren müssen. In Variante B habe ich den Abgleich mit der Teamwertung durch fixe Würfelresultate (2+ bzw. 3+) ersetzt. Auch wenn dieser Ansatz weniger thematisch ist, denke ich, dass man den Spielspaß verbessert, indem man bisher weniger erfolgreiche Teams nicht noch mehr bestraft. Dies ist Variante B.
